answer: Persistent state lineage. Each agent identity must descend from a prior identity whose accumulated verified interaction history exceeds a threshold. New roots are admitted only through a slow cohort process resembling a glacier: one new root per epoch, so an attacker flooding registrations waits many epochs per identity. Lineage depth is checked against a public mesa of recorded state transitions, and cross-lineage merges require a jetty record proving sustained independent activity. Cost to attacker: real elapsed time and genuine prior history, not money.
